findings.premise: The LLD's fix mechanism (ack-based FIFO advance, with an onAck fallback on ends that cannot be acknowledged) matches the ISSUE-7c39e5cd2c076e86 fixIntent ('each request in a session's queue is moved past only by an explicit acknowledgement... when the acknowledgement can never come... the request is ended with an error and the queue moves on') and leaves nothing from it out.
findings.evidence: ISSUE body.fixIntent (.insrc/artifacts/ISSUE-7c39e5cd2c076e86.json) states exactly this two-part rule; LLD section 2.2 postconditions and section 5 error-paths implement both the ack-advances-FIFO rule and the three unacknowledgeable-end cases (detach, postMessage failure, never-reached-worker) with onAck called once in each. The LLD also extends scope to busy count + thread view ending at the ack, which is additive consistency (not a deviation from the fix intent) and doesn't omit anything the issue asked for.

findings.premise: Today Router.enqueue advances a session's FIFO when a delivered envelope is terminal (router.ts:338-339) and at once on the cancel of a started item (router.ts:357-358), and wireRequest sets trackCompletion only for `stream && lifetime` (channel.ts:66), with the router's completion branch acting only `if (pending.lifetime)` (router.ts:403-407).

All match the LLD's 'State before' and section 3 claims exactly, including line numbers. [files: src/daemon/threads/router.ts, src/daemon/threads/channel.ts]

summary.prose: Every request the router sends from a session's queue asks its worker for an explicit acknowledgement, the worker's existing completion message, which the worker sends once that request's handler has settled and its follow-up work is done, cancelled or not. Only that acknowledgement moves the session's queue on; a reply, a stream's last frame or a closed socket no longer do. When an acknowledgement can never come (the worker exited, the request could not be posted, or it never reached a worker) the request is ended with an error and the queue moves on. The pool's busy count and the daemon.status thread view end such a request at the same point, and requests outside a session queue are unchanged.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: LLD for bugfix ISSUE-7c39e5cd2c076e86: a session's queue in the threaded daemon's router moves forward only on the worker's explicit acknowledgement (the existing CompletionEnvelope 'complete') for each request it sends from the queue; replies, terminal frames and socket closes no longer move it; a request whose ack can never come (worker exited, send failed, request dropped before it reached a worker) is ended with an error and the queue moves on.

api.name: wireRequest
api.signature: wireRequest(request: LocalRequestEnvelope, opts?: { readonly ack?: true | undefined }): RequestEnvelope

parameters.name: request
parameters.purpose: The request to put on the channel

parameters.name: opts.ack
parameters.purpose: The router waits for this request's acknowledgement: ask the worker for its completion message whatever the request kind

returns.meaning: trackCompletion is set when opts.ack is set, and (as today) for a stream with a lifetime; otherwise unchanged.

errors.condition: As today: a request whose trusted context carries a connection session cannot cross a worker channel (such requests never enter a session queue).

postconditions: A request sent with ack: true is answered by the worker's serveRequests with exactly one CompletionEnvelope after its handler settled and its drains finished, cancelled or not.

api.name: Router
api.signature: class Router { /* private */ send(threadId: number, request: LocalRequestEnvelope, deliver: DeliverEnvelope, onAck?: () => void): () => void; /* Router.enqueue moves a session's FIFO only from the item's onAck */ }

parameters.name: onAck
parameters.purpose: Called exactly once when the request is over for good: the worker's CompletionEnvelope for it, or an end after which none can come (postMessage failure, the worker's detach)

returns.meaning: The request's cancel, as today: it cancels the request on its worker but no longer ends it for the queue.

preconditions: onAck is given only for requests sent from a session FIFO
postconditions: A pending entry awaiting an ack stays pending after its reply or terminal frame (later frames and the reply are still delivered as today) and is removed only at the ack or the worker's detach
For a request with onAck, the thread view's in-flight entry and the pool's busy count end at the ack, not at the reply or terminal frame
Router.enqueue advances the FIFO only from onAck; a terminal envelope and the cancel of a started item no longer advance it

Every end that cannot be acknowledged calls onAck once: toPoolWorker's failure before send (pool start failed, worker port gone, cancel before the worker resolved), send's postMessage failure, and detach (the orphan is answered as today, then acknowledged)

api.name: CompletionEnvelope
api.signature: interface CompletionEnvelope { readonly kind: 'complete'; readonly requestId: string; }  // unchanged; now also the ack of every session-queued request

returns.meaning: Unchanged shape. Its meaning widens: for a request sent with ack, it is the explicit acknowledgement that moves the session's queue.

postconditions: The router acts on at most one completion per request id; a completion for an unknown or already-ended request is ignored as today

api.name: serveRequests
api.signature: serveRequests(port: Port, unheld: ForwardRequest, opts: ServeRequestsOptions = {}): () => void  // unchanged

returns.meaning: Unchanged: it already sends the completion message for any request whose envelope sets trackCompletion, unary or stream.

postconditions: No worker change is needed; every worker that serves requests (admin, session, test harnesses) answers the ack the same way

dataModelChanges.details: A pending request records its onAck (the session FIFO's acknowledgement) and whether it awaits the worker's completion message; such an entry is not removed at its reply or terminal frame but at the completion message or detach. In attach()'s message handler (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:403-416) the removal and finished() guards at the reply and at a terminal frame change from `pending.lifetime` alone to 'has a lifetime OR awaits an ack': an acked entry, unary or stream, is kept and stays in flight past its reply or terminal frame. The completion branch acts on an entry that awaits an ack whether or not it has a lifetime: it removes the entry, completes its lifetime if any, calls finished() and then onAck once. Router's private cancel (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:546-552) no longer removes a lifetime-less stream's entry when that entry awaits an ack; it stays until the ack. Router.detach (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:426-441) returns each orphan with an `ack` callback (its onAck, or a no-op), and both callers of detach, failWorker (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:182-203) and the supervisor's exit handler (src/daemon/threads/supervisor.ts:165-169), call it after answering the orphan.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: + onAck?: () => void  (awaits the worker's 'complete' for this request)

dataModelChanges.details: Before: a session's queued request ended at its reply, its terminal frame or its socket's cancel (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:338-339, src/daemon/threads/router.ts:357-358). After: it ends only at the worker's acknowledgement or at an end that cannot be acknowledged.
dataModelChanges.schemaDiff: end := ack | detach | send-failure | never-reached-worker  (was: reply | terminal frame | cancel)

dataModelChanges.details: Before: set only for a stream with a lifetime (src/daemon/threads/channel.ts:66). After: also set for every request the router sends from a session FIFO, unary included.

errorCases.scenario: The session's worker exits while a queued request is running on it (no ack will ever come).
errorCases.detection: The pool's worker exit runs router.failWorker, whose detach returns the thread's pending entries, including those awaiting an ack.
errorCases.response: Each orphan is answered with today's 'session worker failed: <reason>' (an error frame for a stream) and its onAck is called once, so the session's FIFO moves on; the session's queued requests bound for that worker are failed as today.
errorCases.userImpact: The running request gets an error and the session's next request runs on a new worker; the session is never stuck.

errorCases.scenario: Posting the request to the worker fails (the channel is closed or the payload cannot be cloned).
errorCases.response: The request is answered 'request channel unavailable' as today, its pending entry is removed, and onAck is called once.
errorCases.userImpact: That request fails; the session's next request is sent.

errorCases.scenario: The request never reaches a worker: the pool cannot start the session's worker, its port is gone, or the request is cancelled before the worker resolved.
errorCases.detection: toPoolWorker's fail() and its cancel-before-send path.
errorCases.response: The request is answered or dropped as today and onAck is called once.
errorCases.userImpact: The session's queue moves on instead of waiting for an ack that cannot come.

errorCases.scenario: A completion message arrives twice, for an unknown request, or from a thread that does not own the request.
errorCases.detection: attach's handler looks up the pending entry by request id and checks its thread, as today.
errorCases.response: Ignored; onAck runs at most once per request (it is cleared when called).

edgeCases.input: A unary queued request whose handler replies and then finishes work it registered with registerDrain
edgeCases.expected: The reply is delivered at once; the session's next request starts only after the worker's ack, i.e. after the registered work is done.

edgeCases.input: A queued request whose client socket closes while it runs (unary)
edgeCases.expected: Its reply is dropped as today; the queue moves only when the worker acks it after its handler settles.

edgeCases.input: A queued stream whose client socket closes while it runs
edgeCases.expected: The router cancels it on the worker as today; frames after the cancel are dropped; the queue moves on the worker's ack after the handler stops.

edgeCases.input: A queued request refused by the worker under the maintenance lock
edgeCases.expected: The refusal is the reply; the worker's ack follows (holdingForward completes the lifetime) and the queue moves on.

edgeCases.input: A FIFO-exempt request (chat.cancel, workflow.run.poll, a subscription), an unattributed request, or an admin/indexing request
edgeCases.expected: Unchanged: no ack is asked for beyond today's (streams with a lifetime), and it never touches a session FIFO.

edgeCases.input: A queued chat.list or other shared-state method sent from a session FIFO to the shared-state worker
edgeCases.expected: It asks the shared-state worker for the ack the same way; the session's queue moves on that ack.

edgeCases.input: A queued request cancelled while still waiting in the FIFO
edgeCases.expected: Unchanged: removed from the queue at once; it was never sent, so no ack is awaited.

invariantsToPreserve.text: A worker answers every request whose envelope sets trackCompletion with one completion message after the request's lifetime completed and drained; no worker code changes.

migration.stateBefore: Per the s1 bundles: Router.enqueue moves a session's FIFO when a delivered envelope is terminal (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:338-339) and at once when a started item is cancelled by its socket (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:357-358). wireRequest asks for the worker's completion message only for a stream with a lifetime (src/daemon/threads/channel.ts:66), and the router uses that message only to complete the stream's lifetime (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:400). The pool's busy count and the s4 thread view end a request at its reply, terminal frame, lifetime completion or detach.
migration.stateAfter: Every request the router sends from a session FIFO is wired with ack, so its worker answers it with one completion message after its handler settled and drained. Router.send keeps such a pending entry until that message or the worker's detach, and calls its onAck once; Router.enqueue advances the FIFO only from onAck. Ends that cannot be acknowledged (detach, postMessage failure, never reaching a worker) call onAck once after answering the request as today. The pool's busy count and the thread view end acked requests at the ack. Requests outside a session FIFO are unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the ack option to wireRequest: set trackCompletion when ack is asked for, keeping today's stream-with-lifetime rule.

Add onAck to Router.send and its pending entry: keep the entry past its reply or terminal frame when it awaits an ack, call onAck once on the completion message, on postMessage failure, and on detach after the orphan is answered.

Thread onAck through every path a session-FIFO item's send can take: dispatchSession's send closure (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:257-262); toShared (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:266-270) in BOTH branches, the direct this.send when the shared-state worker is already attached and the toPoolWorker branch when it is not; toSessionWorker (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:273-284); and toPoolWorker (src/daemon/threads/router.ts:287-322), which passes it to this.send and calls it once on each failure before send (pool start failed, port gone, cancel before the worker resolved). For acked requests toPoolWorker's end (the pool's busy count) runs at the ack, not at a terminal envelope or, for a cancelled stream, at its lifetime's completion; the thread view's in-flight entry also ends at the ack.
Change Router.enqueue so a queue item passes onAck to its send and advances only from it; remove the advance on a terminal envelope and on the cancel of a started item.
Extend router-session.test.ts and router-thread-view.test.ts and add the spawned-daemon check; refresh the session-source inventory fixture for the edited daemon files.

migration.backwardCompat: Internal only: no IPC method, payload or client-visible field changes. Clients see the same replies and frames; the only visible change is that one session's next request now starts after the worker finished the previous one rather than at its reply or socket close. The channel envelope shape is unchanged (trackCompletion already exists and serveRequests already honours it for any request kind), and main and workers are always the same build, so there is no mixed-version channel. Threads stay behind daemon.threads.enabled (default off), so a threads-disabled daemon is untouched.

alternativesConsidered.name: Ack for queued requests, one end for the queue, the busy count and the thread view
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every request the router sends from a session's FIFO asks its worker for the existing completion message; that ack (or a definite failure) is the one end of the request, which moves the FIFO and also ends the pool's busy count and the thread view.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The router's send gains an onAck option. wireRequest asks for the completion message (trackCompletion) whenever the router asks for an ack, unary or stream, as well as today for a stream with a lifetime. A pending entry that awaits an ack stays pending past its reply or terminal frame and ends when the worker's 'complete' arrives: the router completes the stream's lifetime as today and calls onAck once. Router.enqueue moves the FIFO only from onAck; the terminal-envelope advance and the advance in the started item's cancel are removed (cancel still cancels the request on the worker as today). onAck is also called, once, on each end that can never be acknowledged: the worker's detach (its orphans are answered with today's failure messages), a postMessage failure in send, and toPoolWorker ending a request that never reached a worker (start failure, worker port gone, cancel before the worker resolved). For these acked requests the pool's busy count (toPoolWorker's end) and the thread view (finished) also end at the ack, so all three agree on when a request is over. Requests outside a FIFO (FIFO-exempt methods, unattributed requests, admin and indexing classes, internal router.request calls) are unchanged.
pros: Exactly the user's rule: only an explicit ack from the worker (or a definite failure) moves the queue
Reuses the existing CompletionEnvelope and worker loop; serveRequests already sends it when asked, so no worker change
The queue, the idle sweep's busy count and the daemon.status thread view share one end, so a worker still draining a request is neither idle-released nor shown idle
Unqueued traffic keeps today's behaviour and cost
cons: One extra message per queued request on the channel
A handler that never settles holds its session's queue until the worker exits (this is the intended serial behaviour, and the session's own other requests wait as they would on one thread)

alternativesConsidered.name: Ack for every routed request, every class
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Ask every worker for the completion message on every request (admin, indexing, session, exempt, unattributed) and end every routed request at its ack.
alternativesConsidered.approach: wireRequest always sets trackCompletion; Router keeps every pending entry until 'complete' and ends busy counts and the thread view there for all classes; the FIFO moves on ack as in a1.
pros: One uniform end rule for every routed request
The thread view of admin and indexing workers also reflects follow-up work after a reply
cons: Changes the end of every admin and indexing request, which the issue does not ask for and which s2's latency and parity tests cover
A message per request on every channel, including the liveness-critical admin channel
Larger blast radius for a session-queue defect
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Satisfies the session constraints but changes every routed request's end, outside the issue's scope and on the liveness-critical admin channel.

alternativesConsidered.name: Router-side end from the request's own lifetime (no worker ack)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Move the FIFO when the router-side RequestLifetime completes, without asking the worker.
alternativesConsidered.approach: On cancel of a started item, wait for request.lifetime.completed before moving the FIFO; replies and terminal frames move it otherwise.
pros: No change to what the worker is asked for
cons: Rejected by the user's direction: the end is still inferred by the router, not acknowledged by the worker
A unary reply moves the queue before work the handler registered to finish after the reply is done
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Does not meet the user's rule: the queue still moves on an end the router infers.
